questions.question: A savings table has three rows. Every row starts with a principal of $400 in a savings account paying 3% simple interest. Row A is kept for 1 year, Row B for 2 years, and Row C for 6 months. Which row earns the most interest, and how much is it?
options: Row B, with $24 of interest
Row B, with $424 of interest
Row C, with $72 of interest
Row A, with $12 of interest
questions.explain: When principal and rate are the same in every row, the longest time earns the most: 400 × 0.03 × 2 = $24. Watch the 6-month row — that is t = 0.5, not t = 6.

questions.question: A savings table lists three options that all pay 4% simple interest for 6 months. Option A starts with a principal of $300, Option B with $600, and Option C with $900. What is the total amount in Option B at the end of the 6 months?
questions.explain: Six months is 1/2 of a year, so I = 600 × 0.04 × 0.5 = $12, and total = principal + interest = 600 + 12 = $612. The $12 on its own is only the interest, not the account.

questions.question: In a savings table, Row A holds a principal of $800 at 2% simple interest for 6 months, and Row B holds a principal of $800 at 4% simple interest for 6 months. Which statement about these two rows is true?
options: Row B earns $32 and Row A earns $16, so B doubles A
Row B earns $192 and Row A earns $96, so B doubles A
Row B earns $16 and Row A earns $8, so B doubles A
Row B totals $16 and Row A totals $8 after 6 months
questions.explain: With the same principal and time, doubling only the rate doubles the interest: 800 × 0.02 × 0.5 = $8 and 800 × 0.04 × 0.5 = $16. Those amounts are the interest earned; each account still totals over $800.

questions.question: A savings table has four rows, and each row starts with a principal of $500 at 3% simple interest. Row A runs for 4 months, Row B for 6 months, Row C for 12 months, and Row D for 24 months. Which row earns exactly half as much interest as Row C?
options: Row D, because 24 months is twice 12 months
Row A, because 4 months earns $60 when t = 4
Row B, because its interest comes to $507.50
Row B, because 6 months is half of 12 months
questions.explain: With P and r fixed, interest grows in step with time, so half the time gives half the interest: 500 × 0.03 × 0.5 = $7.50, which is half of Row C's $15. The $507.50 is a total, not an interest amount.

questions.question: Account M has P = $900, r = 0.03, t = 2 years. Account N has P = $900, r = 0.06, t = 12 months. Which statement is true?
options: Both earn $54, so both totals are $954
N earns more: $648 against M's $54
N earns more, because 6% is double 3%
Both earn $54, so both totals are $54
questions.explain: Doubling the rate while halving the time leaves I = Prt unchanged: both give $54, and each total is 900 + 54 = $954. Note that 12 months means t = 1, not t = 12.

questions.question: Sofia has $1,200 to put away. Bank A pays 2.5% simple interest for 2 years, and Bank B pays 4% simple interest for 9 months. Which bank leaves her with the bigger total, and what is that total?
options: Bank B, $1,632
Bank A, $1,260
Bank A, $60
Bank B, $1,236
questions.explain: Find each total: Bank A gives 1200 + 1200 × 0.025 × 2 = $1,260, and Bank B gives 1200 + 1200 × 0.04 × 0.75 = $1,236. The higher rate does not win here, because 9 months is only 0.75 of a year.

questions.question: A savings account has P = $2,000, r = 0.035 and t = 1 year, so I = $70. A second account keeps the same rate and the same time but starts with three times the principal. What total will the second account hold at the end of the year?
questions.explain: Tripling the principal triples the interest, 3 × $70 = $210, and the total is the new principal plus that interest: 6000 + 210 = $6,210. The interest alone is never the final amount.

questions.question: Rowan has $600 of birthday money to save. Which plan leaves him with the most money at the end of its term?
options: 5% for 9 months, ending with $622.50
9% for 6 months, ending with $924
4% for 18 months, ending with $36
4% for 18 months, ending with $636

questions.question: Priya deposits $750 in a savings account paying 3% simple interest and leaves it there for 8 months. She writes I = 750 × 0.03 × 8 and gets $180. Judge her work.
options: The interest is $15, since 8 months is 8/12 of a year
The $180 is right, since time can be counted in months
The interest is $765, since the principal must be added
The interest is $22.50, since a rate is always yearly
questions.explain: Time in I = Prt must be written in years, so 8 months is 8/12 = 2/3 of a year: 750 × 0.03 × 2/3 = $15. Using t = 8 makes the interest twelve times too large.

questions.question: Nolan saved $480 from his paper route. His credit union offers 2% simple interest for 3 years, while a savings bond offers 5% simple interest for 9 months. Which option earns more interest, and by how much?
options: The bond, by $187.20 of interest
The credit union, by $10.80 of interest
The bond, since 5% is far above 2%
The credit union, by $508.80 of interest
questions.explain: Compare the interest, not the rates: 480 × 0.02 × 3 = $28.80 against 480 × 0.05 × 0.75 = $18, so the credit union earns $10.80 more. Nine months is 0.75 of a year, and $508.80 is a total, not interest.

questions.question: Maya already has $250 in her savings account. On the first day of the term she deposits her $90 birthday money into the same account, then leaves it untouched for 18 months at 4% simple interest. How much money is in the account at the end?
questions.explain: Record the deposit first, so the principal is 250 + 90 = $340, then I = 340 × 0.04 × 1.5 = $20.40 and the account holds 340 + 20.40 = $360.40. The $20.40 is only the interest earned.

questions.question: Jae has $1,000 and two savings options. Option 1 pays 6% simple interest for 2 years; Option 2 pays 4% simple interest for 3 years. Jae says Option 2 must be better because it runs for more years. Is Jae right?
options: Yes, because more years always beat a higher rate
No, Option 1 wins, since 6% always beats 4%
No, Option 2 earns $1,120 of interest and wins
No, both earn $120, so the totals tie
questions.explain: Rate and time act together in I = Prt: 1000 × 0.06 × 2 = $120 and 1000 × 0.04 × 3 = $120, so both accounts end at $1,120. A longer time only wins if the lower rate does not cancel it out.
